description: Symbolic MIDI exercises, with separately attributed lyric presets in lyric-presets.mjs, minyo-lyrics.mjs and folk-lyrics.mjs. Traditional Tinsagu/Tsukinu verses1–3, Aha first stanza, Akata/Tancha reading companions and existing PD English stanzas are documented in lyrics-provenance.json. No recordings, samples, Asatoya lyrics or modern song lyrics.

songs.title: Amazing Grace
songs.attribution: Trad. / Arr.: Breizh Partitions, typeset by Breizh Partitions (2012), via Mutopia Project, piece 1832.
songs.changes: Removed short bagpipe grace notes; extended each main note to the next onset; transposed down 8 semitones to G; tempo 90; added suggested G/C/D chord markers. This adapted MIDI and its note data retain CC BY-SA 3.0. App code is separate.

lyrics.scope: Existing public-domain English stanza only. MIDI contains no lyric events; the words are a separate app preset.

songs.title: きらきら星
songs.composer: Traditional French melody (Ah! vous dirai-je, maman)
songs.attribution: Traditional melody, newly entered as a simple 42-note exercise by Music Stack. The linked public-domain edition is a reference, not the imported arrangement.
songs.changes: New symbolic transcription of the traditional melody in C, tempo 90, for sanshin honchoshi and guitar. Added suggested C/Fmaj7/G7 chord markers. MIDI contains no lyric events; the English text is a separate credited app preset.

lyrics.scope: Existing public-domain English stanza only. MIDI contains no lyric events; the words are a separate app preset.

songs.title: 歓喜の歌（主題）
songs.attribution: Beethoven's public-domain theme, newly entered as a 30-note beginner exercise by Music Stack. The linked Mutopia public-domain SATB edition is a reference; its arrangement was not imported.
songs.changes: New symbolic transcription of the opening theme in C, tempo 90, with suggested C/G7 chord markers. No lyrics or recordings.

songs.title: てぃんさぐぬ花（1節・やさしい版）
songs.attribution: Kunkunshi for Tinsagu nu Hana, Lrschneider (2017), Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0. Adaptation by Music Stack.
songs.changes: First verse with surrounding instrumental phrase. Transcribed the large symbols right-to-left, top-to-bottom; omitted small ornamental notes, set each cell to one beat at 85 BPM in C-F-C honchoshi. Retains the one-cell rest. 63 notes across 64 beats. This adapted MIDI and the note data in build-practice-sanshin.mjs retain CC BY-SA 4.0; application code is separate. The symbolic MIDI has no lyric events; traditional verses1–3 are separate credited app presets. No source image is bundled.

lyric_extension_v42.note: Lyrics are separate presets; the one-verse symbolic MIDI bytes are unchanged. Choose one verse at a time. See lyrics-provenance.json.

songs.title: 安里屋ゆんた（前奏＋1節・基礎練習版）
songs.composer: 宮良長包 (Chohu Miyara, 1883–1939), based on the traditional Yaeyama song
songs.scope: New monophonic elementary study: introduction and one verse, honchoshi C–F–C, uniform one-beat cells at 85 BPM and a two-beat final note. It is a beginner practice arrangement, not a synchronization or full transcription of a teacher's recording.
songs.license_scope: Music Stack dedicates its newly entered symbolic MIDI and elementary study arrangement to CC0. This does not license third-party sheet layouts, lyrics, recordings, or teaching arrangements.

rights_basis.composer_fact: The Miyara Chohu Association records the composer's death on 1939-06-29 and lists Asatoya Yunta among his works.
rights_basis.term_basis: The composer's underlying published melody is public domain in Japan. The 2018 term extension does not revive expired copyrights. Modern publisher and performer contributions are not covered by that status.

melody_cross_checks.credit: 伊禮俊一・公式初心者レッスン
melody_cross_checks.use: Cross-check the basic introduction, first-verse pitch contours and honchoshi relation. No lyrics, files, recording or publisher layout bundled.

melody_cross_checks.credit: 宮里英克沖縄三線教室・公開教材
melody_cross_checks.use: Visual cross-check of common melody phrases and honchoshi. Publisher PDF, lyrics, compact ornaments, strike annotations and distinct performance phrasing are not bundled.

songs.changes: New plain-symbol practice entry using the basic shared melody. Straight one-beat durations replace expressive phrasing; ornamental strikes and compressed clusters are omitted, one verse is used, section pauses and a held final note are added. Guide sound is synthesized by the existing instrument voice. For authentic timing, ornament and singing, use the linked teacher lesson.
songs.lyrics: No lyric text is bundled. Existing teacher video/PDF references and local personal lyric entry remain available.

songs.title: 月ぬ美しゃ（1節と囃子・本調子のやさしい版）
songs.composer: Traditional Yaeyama lullaby; no modern songwriter credited for the underlying traditional melody or first-verse words
songs.scope: New elementary monophonic study: introduction, first verse and refrain. Honchoshi C–F–C, straight one-beat cells at 85 BPM, four one-beat rests and a two-beat final note. This is not a synchronization to a recording or the complete arrangement of an Apple Music track.
songs.license_scope: Music Stack dedicates its newly entered symbolic MIDI, elementary honchoshi arrangement, phonetic alignment and original short meanings to CC0. Traditional words and underlying melody are public domain. Third-party score layouts, performances, distinctive ornaments and modern translations are excluded.

rights_basis.fact: Kyoiku Geijutsu identifies this as a traditional Yaeyama lullaby sung by girls caring for children, gives the traditional first-verse words, explains their meaning and identifies the Hoi Choga refrain. No modern Japanese lyric adaptation is used.

melody_reference.credit: 豊岡マッシー・三線教室 ONLINE 東京
melody_reference.use: Identify the common traditional first-verse and refrain pitch contour. The source uses niage; our new study uses equivalent pitches with easy honchoshi positions (niage shi→honchoshi jo, niage jo→honchoshi chu, low fa→honchoshi shi). Small ornaments, source layout, finger choices, printed rendition and expressive rhythm are not reproduced.

songs.changes: Newly entered beginner honchoshi study. Main traditional melody only, uniform durations, omitted small ornaments, open middle string for the final low fa, held final note. First verse and refrain only. Phrase and phonetic cues refer exclusively to this study, not the linked teacher video. Guide sound uses the existing synthesized instrument voice; no recording is added.
songs.lyrics: Traditional first verse and Hoi Choga refrain. Readings are one practical example; regional pronunciation and spelling vary. The app's short meanings are newly written paraphrases, not copied modern translations.

lyric_extension_v42.note: Lyrics are separate presets; the one-verse symbolic MIDI bytes are unchanged. Choose one verse at a time. See lyrics-provenance.json.

songs.title: 安波節（1番・本調子の基礎練習）
songs.author: Traditional; newly entered elementary study by Music Stack
songs.source: https://ks-sanshin.com/youtubeチャンネルに「安波節」を追加しました♪～歌/
songs.scope: Traditional first stanza, two matching upper/lower-phrase cycles. Honchoshi C–F–C; one cell per beat, omitted small ornaments and vocal Hari inflections, two-beat final note. A new practice rendering, not a recording transcription.

rights_basis.source: https://ks-sanshin.com/youtubeチャンネルに「安波節」を追加しました♪～歌/
rights_basis.fact: The performing teacher identifies the song as handed down in Aha, Kunigami and used for celebrations. A 1993 Ryukyu University teaching paper p265 independently shows the same basic traditional contour and explains its beginner suitability.

comparison_sources.use: Basic contour comparison; modern vocal inflections, layout and translation excluded.

songs.changes: New symbolic entry of common large-note contour. Omit small intra-cell notes; repeat the basic cycle for the lower couplet as indicated by the traditional lower-couplet instruction. Align first words to the preceding sounding cell at beats8/61 rather than a vocal onset on rest9/62. New original readings, easy meanings and vocabulary. Equal beats do not reproduce a teacher performance.
songs.lyrics: Traditional first stanza only, separately attributed preset song:aha. Readings are an example; regional variations exist. No modern translation copied.
